flawed_step: Step 2: going from P(X>Y)>1/2 and P(Y>Z)>1/2 to P(X>Z)>1/2. Independence gives no inequality linking these probabilities, so this step cannot be justified (non-transitive dice).
counterexample: X, Y, Z independent, each uniform on three values: X on {2,4,9}, Y on {1,6,8}, Z on {3,5,7}. P(X>Y)=5/9, P(Y>Z)=5/9, but P(X>Z)=4/9 (so Z beats X).
assessment_summary: The claim is false. With non-transitive dice X on {2,4,9}, Y on {1,6,8} and Z on {3,5,7} (independent, each uniform), X beats Y with 5/9 and Y beats Z with 5/9, but P(X>Z)=4/9 < 1/2.
